taxonomic_note: Accepted POWO/FNA species; Coleosanthus cylindraceus is a synonym. Do not infer varieties from species-only material.
look_here_first: Examine paired nodes and the underside of a mature leaf: leaves often opposite or nearly opposite, densely pale-tomentose beneath and gland-dotted. Confirm on a head by checking layered phyllaries; the outer bracts are at most about half the inner length. Do not identify by stream-gravel habitat alone.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Approved Master Plant Pool row 157; taxonomy and diagnostics reviewed 2026-10-09
project_inclusion.range_basis: Texas-native at state scale in POWO; no completed BONAP/NAPA-first three-target-county certification for this batch. Native-only metrics excluded.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial woody-based shrub, often on gravel bars or rocky sites; habitat is supportive, not diagnostic.
morphology_keys.leaves: Leaves often opposite or subopposite, abaxial surface densely tomentose and gland-dotted; inspect intact nodes and both leaf faces.
morphology_keys.flowers: Discoid heads, typically 18–22 phyllaries in 5–7 series; involucres about 8–13 mm; outer phyllaries no more than half the inner length.
morphology_keys.fruits: Check mature cypsela pubescence; often hairy relative to usually glabrous B. dentata.
best_field_traits: paired or nearly paired leaf nodes

comparisons.key_distinctions: Brickellia dentata (alternate leaves, often coarsely toothed, mature cypselae usually glabrous); Brickellia eupatorioides (plumose or subplumose pappus; species complex with variable phyllotaxy); Brickellia lemmonii and B. conduplicata overlap in vegetative characters. Use head and fruit together.
